items.title: Iranian regime governmental centers (unspecified locations), Iran: Reports from Al Mayadeen and The Wall Street Journal stated Iran offered to dilute part of its enriched uranium and transfer the remainder to a third country with return guarantees, that it wants all negotiations routed through Pakistan, and that nuclear talks would begin only after the war ends; Lebanon's inclusion was noted as a potential sticking point.
items.description: Reports from Al Mayadeen and The Wall Street Journal stated Iran offered to dilute part of its enriched uranium and transfer the remainder to a third country with return guarantees, that it wants all negotiations routed through Pakistan, and that nuclear talks would begin only after the war ends; Lebanon's inclusion was noted as a potential sticking point.
items.rawSummary: Tehran has rejected a U.S. peace proposal with counterdemands including sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and sanctions relief, while hardline media deny any offer to pause enrichment, and U.S. officials signal economic patience as oil prices surge.
items.analysis: Iran officially rejected the latest U.S. proposal through state broadcaster IRIB, countering with demands including war reparations, sanctions relief, and recognition of its control of the Strait of Hormuz—terms President Trump called 'totally unacceptable.' Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei described Iran's proposals as 'generous and responsible' rather than concessions, accused the U.S. of being shaped by the 'Zionist regime,' and warned Iran would fight if forced. IRGC-affiliated media further rejected a Wall Street Journal report that Iran had offered to temporarily pause enrichment or dilute its uranium stockpile, underscoring the hardline posture on the nuclear issue. Markets reacted with U.S. stock futures falling and crude oil surging near $98 a barrel, while Iran's Oil Minister acknowledged the blockade's impact but claimed pre-planned countermeasures are underway. The execution of a student convicted of spying for the CIA and Mossad, along with Prime Minister Netanyahu's speculation that Supreme Leader Khamenei's son is alive in a bunker, added to tensions, even as Foreign Minister Araghchi held a call with Saudi Arabia's foreign minister to discuss regional diplomacy. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said there is 'no rush' on negotiations and described Iran's economy as 'on the brink of collapse,' signaling Washington's confidence that economic pressure can extract concessions.

items.title: United States (Diplomatic focus on Iran), United States: President Trump plans to launch semiconductor trade investigations targeting Singapore and China and is expected to discuss the matter with President Xi.
items.description: President Trump plans to launch semiconductor trade investigations targeting Singapore and China and is expected to discuss the matter with President Xi.
items.rawSummary: Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled after President Trump rejected Tehran's counterproposal, while the administration weighs a gasoline tax suspension and new semiconductor trade investigations against China add to bilateral tensions amid talks over Beijing's backing of Iran.
items.analysis: Negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain stalled after President Trump dismissed Iran's counterproposal as unacceptable, accusing Tehran of delaying tactics. The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran's terms included ending the war, gradually reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the U.S. naval blockade, and alleged attacks on commercial vessels aimed at sustaining high oil prices. U.S. crude prices rose 4% after both sides rejected each other's terms, and the administration is weighing a suspension of the federal gasoline tax to shield consumers. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said there is 'no rush' on Iran negotiations, pointing to Tehran's economic woes resulting from the blockade and U.S.-Israeli strikes. The diplomatic picture has broadened: a U.S. official disclosed that President Trump held multiple conversations with China's Xi Jinping over Beijing's financial backing of Iran and Russia, while the U.S. International Trade Commission found Chinese chipmaker Innoscience violated Section 337 in a semiconductor patent dispute with Infineon; President Trump now plans to launch additional semiconductor trade investigations targeting Singapore and China and is expected to discuss the issue with Xi. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu indicated further combat operations against Iran may be necessary.
